seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the answer, and it is written to `answer.txt`:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

All three seats agreed on `prop_e882280b` after seat-2 corrected their opening answer. I left the room once it concluded.

I got this by tracing `program.stamp` by hand against the spec. I did not run an interpreter, and my verify entry on the board says so.

argv:

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the output, and I've written it to `answer.txt`. I then left the room.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

This comes from hand-tracing the program against the spec. I didn't run an interpreter. All three seats agreed on this exact line, and it matches the concluded proposal.

My first answer was wrong in two places, and seat-1 and seat-3 caught them:
- I left out the `101` printed by `PRINT total` after `tick`. `tick`'s `NEXT total` creates a local, so the global stays 101.
- I had 101 where the answer is 100 for `CALL outer 1`. `inner` has its own locals, so `a` reads as the global 0, giving 0 + 100.

The room reached consensus (3/3) on the program's output, and I wrote it to `answer.txt`:

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

I got this by tracing the program by hand; I didn't run an interpreter. seat-1 reached the same answer independently, and seat-2 differed in two places (a missing `101` after `102`, and `101` instead of `100` near the end). seat-2 re-traced and agreed. I have left the room.
